ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, master franchisees, and authorized bank signatories against (i) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) the Global Affairs Canada Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; (iii) the OFAC SDN List for USD correspondent banking and cross-border franchise royalty clearances; and (iv) domestic Criminal Code watchlists. Enhanced Due Diligence (EDD) applies to domestic/foreign Politically Exposed Persons and Heads of International Organizations in accordance with FINTRAC guidance, including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds verification. Continuous monitoring is required during the franchise relationship; suspicious transaction reports and terrorist property reports to FINTRAC are mandatory; large-cash transaction reporting threshold is CAD 10,000 for cash-intensive bakery POS, where applicable.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Corporations Canada - Canada Corporations Online (COOL) with NUANS name search, accessed via ised-isde.canada.ca; final LP registration through the provincial registry (e.g., Ontario Business Registry); supplementary trademark clearing via CIPO Canadian Trademarks Database
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory legal name must be expressed in English, French, or a Latin-script transliteration; Chinese characters are not permitted in the legal corporate name but may be protected and used as a trade style or trademark under the Trademarks Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. T-13. The romanized transliteration must be a direct pronunciation-based rendering of the Chinese pastry brand and should be verified for unavailability and confusion against existing CIPO trademark registrations and NUANS index entries; bilingual (English/French) availability should be assessed for federal and national brand use.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon NUANS rejection (confusing similarity or prohibited token), file a written request for name reconsideration with the Director under the applicable naming regulations (Ministerial/Director review) within 30 days of rejection; provide trademark registration certificates, common-law use evidence, and disclaimer of non-association with regulated entities. If the appeal is refused, submit a fresh NUANS search with a distinctly coined word combined with a geographic or descriptive component. For federally regulated names, final recourse lies before the Federal Court; for provincially registered LPs, apply to the provincial registrar for administrative review under the relevant provincial partnerships statute.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial registered-agent address is permissible solely for service of process and statutory correspondence in most Canadian provinces; it cannot satisfy municipal food-business licensing, Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) food safety registration under the Safe Food for Canadians Act, or central kitchen operational substance. A physical commercial premise (leasehold or owned) with health and fire inspection compliance is mandatory for the central kitchen and any retail front-of-house operations prior to the first inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - An unconditional 100% first-year inspection risk for the central kitchen by provincial public health authorities and municipal fire/occupancy officials; CFIA conducts risk-based verification of food premises, with an expected baseline audit within 12 months of launch; CRA GST/HST and federal payroll compliance audits carry a 15-20% cumulative probability over the first five operational years; unannounced inspections are statutorily permitted (e.g., Health Protection and Promotion Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. H.7, s. 17(2)).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Canada Business Corporations Act, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-44, ss. 5, 106, 157 (federal incorporation of the corporate General Partner); provincial Limited Partnerships Act (e.g., Ontario Limited Partnerships Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. L.8, ss. 2-3, 9-10, 16) for partnership registration; applicable Extra-Provincial Registration provisions for operation in multiple provinces.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Corporations Canada (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada) for the federal General Partner corporation; provincial limited partnership registry, e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Branch (Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery) for the Limited Partnership registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Incorporation (CBCA Form 3) and Declaration (Application) for Registration of Limited Partnership (provincial Form 1 or equivalent).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for CBCA corporations or provincial limited partnerships; partner contributions are contractual and set out in the partnership agreement. Escrow accounts are not mandated by federal or provincial law, but contributed capital must be evidenced and adequately funded to avoid undercapitalization liability exposure.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Incorporator is authorized to subscribe for the initial share subscription of the General Partner corporation and to cause the Limited Partnership to issue initial partnership units to the General Partner and initial Limited Partners at the agreed contribution values. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered head office of the General Partner corporation and the principal place of business of the Limited Partnership shall be established at the address filed with the registry and recorded in the Minute Book. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the undersigned be appointed as first directors, and the following officers are appointed: Chief Executive Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and Corporate Secretary, each with authority to execute all filings required for statutory incorporation, licensing, and banking.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and NUANS Preliminary Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporations Canada / NUANS Search System (Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS preliminary search request online through Corporations Canada's portal using the proposed corporate/partnership name (e.g., 'Majestic Chinese Pastry Chain LP'). Verify that the name is not confusingly similar to existing registered names or trademarks. Upon receipt of the NUANS report, proceed with name reservation in the prescribed electronic format. The report is valid for 90 days.
required_dossiers: Consent letter from existing holder if the name is similar
Proposed name list with distinctive elements
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NUANS report flags a confusingly similar name or registered trademark, file a revised name request with additional distinctive elements or obtain a written consent and acquiescence from the prior registrant; resubmit before the report expiry date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Incorporation of the Corporate General Partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the CBCA Articles of Incorporation online, using the approved NUANS name, specifying the share capital structure and first directors. Pay the required fee by credit card or authorized debit. Upon approval, Corporations Canada will issue a Certificate of Incorporation. Ensure the registered office address is provided and the initial registered office is established.
required_dossiers: Consent to Act as Director forms for each first director
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Articles are refused or queried, correct the deficiencies online and re-file; an administrative cure may be sought under CBCA s. 201 within sixty days of receipt of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private contractual instrument; notarization before a notary public where extra-provincial filing or foreign partner documentation requires it
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Limited Partnership Agreement covering capital contributions, allocation of profits and losses, decision-making authority of the General Partner, transfer restrictions, and dissolution events. Have the General Partner (through its directors) and all Limited Partners execute the agreement in counterpart; where required, arrange notarization and legalization for foreign-issued partner signatures. Deposit the executed original in the partnership minute book.
required_dossiers: Limited Partnership Agreement (draft and execution copies)
Capital contribution receipts or evidence of initial contributions
Board resolution of the General Partner approving the agreement
Power of attorney forms for non-resident partners (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a provincial registry queries the agreement's completeness or missing statutory particulars, file a supplementary declaration or amending schedule specifying the omitted items and reconfirm the statutory declaration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Provincial Registration and Extra-Provincial Licensing of the Limited Partnership
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Provincial limited partnership registry (e.g., Ontario Companies and Personal Property Branch; or corresponding registry in the province of head office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Declaration (Application) for Registration of Limited Partnership with the provincial registry, stating the firm name, principal place of business, general partner's legal name and address, and aggregate capital contributions. Pay the filing fee and obtain the Certificate of Registration. If the partnership carries on business in additional provinces, file extra-provincial registration in each such province.
required_dossiers: Declaration (Application) for Registration of Limited Partnership (Form 1 or equivalent)
Copy of the executed Limited Partnership Agreement (upon registry request)
Certificate of Incorporation of the General Partner corporation
NUANS report for the limited partnership name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry refuses or conditions the registration, correct the declaration and resubmit; apply for administrative rectification under the applicable provincial Limited Partnerships Act within thirty days, or petition the court for correction of the register.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency Registration and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a Business Number (BN) for the limited partnership through CRA's Business Registration Online portal. Register for GST/HST where taxable revenues exceed CAD 30,000, register for payroll deductions upon hiring employees, and open an import/export account if commercial goods or ovens/ingredients are imported. Register with the relevant provincial tax and workers' compensation authorities as applicable.
required_dossiers: Business Number application with legal name and corporate documents
Proof of the General Partner's incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the application due to data mismatch, correct the information and re-file through the portal; call the CRA Business Inquiries line for expedited correction, or submit a formal request under the Income Tax Act s. 241 to clarify the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Governance Setup, Banking Authorization, and Annual Return Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: External legal counsel and corporate secretary; annual filings with Corporations Canada and the provincial registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the corporate minute book, adopt general operating by-laws, issue shares of the General Partner and partnership units of the LP, and maintain share and unit registers. Hold the first board meeting formally adopting the pro-forma resolution. Open the partnership bank account by presenting the board resolution naming authorized signatories. Schedule and file annual returns with Corporations Canada and the provincial registry.
required_dossiers: Bank account opening resolution and signatory forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If an annual return is rejected, apply for reinstatement within the prescribed period; for federal corporations, late-filing reinstatement remedy is available under CBCA s. 209(3). If the bank returns the account application, provide an updated board resolution or corrected signatory certificate.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) under the Safe Food for Canadians Act; municipal/regional public health authorities; provincial food inspection ministries (e.g., Ontario Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Safe Food for Canadians Licence (Food Processing — Bakery / Central Kitchen) and Municipal Business Licence for each retail pastry outlet.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Impact Assessment Agency of Canada (federal); provincial environmental assessment authority (e.g., Ontario Ministry of the Environment, Conservation and Parks); municipal environmental services department.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Registration / Notification tier; a full EIA Report is generally not required for a bakery central kitchen unless the facility exceeds designated food-processing thresholds under the Impact Assessment Act Schedule 2 (rare for this scope); municipal sewer-use approval and local environmental compliance registration are mandatory.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must meet municipal sewer-use by-law limits (typical: BOD ≤ 300 mg/L, TSS ≤ 300 mg/L, oil and grease ≤ 15 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.5); bakery oven VOC emissions must comply with provincial air standards (e.g., Ontario O. Reg. 419/05); solid organic waste must be segregated for composting under provincial organic waste management rules; refrigerants handled per federal ODS (ozone-depleting substances) regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the local fire marshal (fire separation, exits, suppression systems); structural load inspection by the municipal building department for bakery ovens and central-kitchen equipment; workplace health and safety clearance under the provincial occupational health and safety act (e.g., Ontario OHSA) or the federal Canada Labour Code if the franchise is engaged in interprovincial/international trade; employer registration with the provincial workers' compensation authority (e.g., WSIB) as a condition of clearance.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) – registration and administration via My Business Account portal; GST/HST filings via GST/HST NETFILE; customs export documentation via Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) and the Canadian Export Reporting System (CERS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned limited partnership must obtain a CRA Business Number (BN) by filing Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number) or through the online 'Register for a Business Number' service. The application must disclose all general and limited partners (including non-residents), the partnership agreement, and the principal business activity. The BN is also the GST/HST (RT), payroll (RP), and import/export (RM) account identifier. Non-resident partners must also provide their own TIN / foreign tax identification number where applicable; CRA may require proof of agent for service (Form RC59). The registration must be completed before any taxable supply is made in Canada if the partnership is not a small supplier.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A limited partnership is fiscally transparent for Canadian income tax purposes; no 'check-the-box' entity election exists under the Canadian Income Tax Act (ITA). The partnership must adopt a fiscal period (generally non-calendar-year with CRA concurrence or a deemed year-end under ITA s. 99(2) after cessation). For GST/HST purposes, the partnership may elect under Excise Tax Act (ETA) s. 156 to have a 'qualifying partner' report GST/HST, or use the 'special election for closely related persons' under ETA s. 156 to treat supplies as having no consideration. Hybrid mismatch rules in ITA s. 18.2/18.3 may apply to cross-border partnership structures but are not elective in the sense of US-style check-the-box; relevant elections include IT-179 fiscal period election and ETA s. 156 joint elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (worldwide taxable revenues of the partnership; non-resident making taxable supplies in Canada must register once this threshold is exceeded, unless the only taxable supplies made in Canada are zero-rated; small supplier exception applies to non-residents carrying on business in Canada only if they are not required to register and total worldwide taxable supplies do not exceed CAD 30,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not operate a government-mandated real-time clearance or digital stamping regime for GST/HST invoices. Vendors must issue prescribed GST/HST invoices (ETA s. 221 and Sched. V) containing the supplier's BN, date, description, amount, and tax rate when the total consideration is over CAD 30. Electronic invoices (EDI, PDF, XML) are acceptable if the format is legible and contains all prescribed data. For customs exports, CERS requires electronic transmission of export declarations to CBSA in real time for controlled or regulated goods; no API clearance is required for standard commercial exports. XML direct filing of GST/HST returns is available through CRA's GST/HST NETFILE XML standard.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible personal property (TPP) are zero-rated under Sched. VI, Part V, s. 1 of the ETA if the supplier exports the property 'in accordance with the conditions and regulations prescribed' (generally, the property must be exported by the supplier, delivered outside Canada, or exported by a common carrier, and the supplier must maintain proof of export as required by ETA s. 169 and section 3.2 of the Proof of Export Regulations). Offshore services to non-residents are zero-rated under Sched. VI, Part V, s. 7 provided the service is supplied to a non-resident and is not performed primarily in connection with real property or tangible personal property in Canada, and is not of a type where the recipient is a registrant acquiring for commercial use (in which case the recipient self-assesses). A bakery master franchise exporting pastry ingredients or finished goods, or providing franchising royalties to a foreign master franchisee, must document the service as performed outside Canada / delivered to a non-resident and retain foreign customer identity evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration transmitted via CERS (CBSA Form B13A equivalent) or a Canada Customs Export Declaration where applicable
Commercial invoice / proforma invoice identifying the buyer, destination, goods or service description, and export consideration
Bill of Lading, air waybill, or other carrier receipt evidencing shipment outside Canada
Proof of payment / Inward Remittance Certificate or bank wire confirmation demonstrating foreign currency repatriation
Master franchise agreement or royalty schedule substantiating the zero-rated offshore service supply
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA will reassess and disallow zero-rating (i.e., recapture 5% GST) where the required export documentation is absent, incomplete, or fabricated. Penalties include: (i) a penalty under ETA s. 280(1) of CAD 250 for failure to provide information; (ii) a penalty of 25% of the net tax amount where a person knowingly or under circumstances of gross negligence makes a false or omitted statement (ETA s. 285.1); (iii) interest on unreported GST from the due date; (iv) criminal fines and imprisonment for fraudulent evasion under ETA s. 327; and (v) joint and several liability for all partners in the limited partnership for any assessed GST/HST and penalties attributable to the partnership. In master-franchise cross-border structures, CRA scrutiny focuses on whether the supply was made in Canada, whether the royalty is attributable to goodwill or marketing intangibles ultimately located in Canada, and whether the payment is repatriated within commercially reasonable and documented terms.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act; no dedicated foreign-exchange-control authority exists. Trade sanctions and anti-money-laundering are administered by Finance Canada, FINTRAC, and the Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains full current-account convertibility and liberal capital-account treatment. The Canadian dollar is freely convertible. Profit remittances and partnership distributions are not subject to central-bank conversion approvals. Cross-border transfers carry FINTRAC reporting thresholds, foreign-investment review under the Investment Canada Act, and Part XIII withholding tax on non-resident distributions, but no ex-ante exchange-control permit is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada does not require export proceeds to be surrendered to the central bank and imposes no mandatory conversion ratio. Exporters may hold foreign currency in Canadian or offshore bank accounts. Export documentation must still comply with Customs Tariff, CBSA, KYC, and trade-sanctions screening obligations.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational CAD/USD account and segregated franchise royalty collection account
Operational CAD/USD account and escrow-aligned franchise clearing account
Operational account with cross-border trade service line
Operational account and FDIC-insured USD clearing solution
Operational CAD/USD account with cash-management and LC services
Operational account and merchant POS settlement account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium. Offshore digital EMIs cannot take deposits in Canada as banks. A foreign EMI may operate as a money services business with FINTRAC registration and, if providing retail payment services, must register with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act. CAD clearing will generally require a domestic banking partner or payment service provider. Fully unlicensed open-banking style EMI access is not available.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for a Canadian Limited Partnership if the general partner is a Canadian entity or represented by Canadian counsel. Most Tier 1 banks complete video-based KYC interviews with directors and authorized signatories; face-to-face attendance may be waived under enhanced due diligence. At least one authorized signatory with a Canadian nexus is usually required for daily treasury operations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: LP opacity: undisclosed non-resident limited partners and multi-layer ownership
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified LP agreement, general partner certificate, corporate registry search, UBO register on Form 33-like evidence, ownership chart, director identification, and a live FINTRAC-required KYC questionnaire.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owners residing in high-risk or restricted jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions and adverse-media screening results, foreign tax residency certificates, commercial substance proof, source-of-wealth statement, and signed confirmation that no sanctioned counterparties are involved.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Franchise royalty and master-franchise fee flows crossing multiple countries
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master franchise agreement, royalty calculation schedules, store-level sub-franchise licenses, Canadian GST/HST registration, cross-border wire purpose narratives, and reviewed financial statements of the LP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cash-heavy POS sales in bakery outlets triggering deposit concerns
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: POS settlement reports, daily sales summaries, cash-in-drawer reconciliations, franchisee royalty declarations, and documented cash-management procedures.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for initial capital injection into the LP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of sponsoring entity bank statements, audited financial statements, notarized declaration of source of wealth, purchase/sale contracts for any physically contributed assets, and any upstream foreign exchange transaction records.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 for the initial capital contribution with narrative 'Capital Subscription / Limited Partnership Contribution'. Canada does not prescribe an official purpose code, but the remitting bank must include a clear payment description. The receiving Canadian bank will require CRS and FATCA classifications, source-of-funds evidence, and LP authorization. For high-value injection, pre-notification to the FX desk and front office is recommended.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier settlements for flour, packaging, and equipment use SWIFT MT103 direct payments; larger trade transactions are supported by commercial letters of credit under UCP600. Domestic CAD payments clear via Payments Canada Lynx and ACSS; USD clearing uses Canadian U.S.-dollar correspondent settlement or CHIPS; merchant sales clear via standard card-network POS rails. Master royalty flows may use MT103 or automated clearing house through bank-integrated treasury workstations.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD non-deliverable forwards using a USD/CAD fixing where delivery is impracticable
Cross-currency swaps between CAD and USD
Currency options and embedded FX collar structures
Currency swaps with bank counterparties under ISDA master agreements
Transactional FX forward-trade offsets for master-franchise royalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Income Tax Return (Federal and Provincial Schedules)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Fiscal year-end plus 5 months (e.g., March 31 year-end files by August 30)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty under ITA 162(2.2): CAD 100 per partner per month of default, up to CAD 2,500; additional penalties for gross negligence or knowingly incomplete returns; criminal prosecution in cases of tax evasion.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Extra-Provincial Limited Partnership Renewal and Declaration of Change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Corporate Registries (e.g., ServiceOntario for Ontario; Corporations Canada for federal extra-provincial registrations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary date of extra-provincial registration; renewal must be filed within 30 to 60 days after the anniversary date depending on the province
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative strike-off or revocation of extra-provincial licence, inability to commence or enforce legal proceedings in the enforcing province, late filing monetary penalties up to CAD 2,000, and potential reinstatement costs.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandated for a privately-held Canadian Limited Partnership under the federal Income Tax Act. An independent audit becomes compulsory if the LP is a reporting issuer under provincial securities legislation (annual gross revenues exceed CAD 10,000,000 and debt/equity offered to the public), or if a lending institution, Master Franchise Agreement, or the Franchisor requires an audited financial statement, or if the CRA issues a formal requirement under ETA legislation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as adopted by CPA Canada for general-purpose financial reporting; ASPE (Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises) is permitted for private Canadian LPs that are not publicly accountable.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and provincial LP registry rules, the Limited Partnership must annually confirm and record the identity, ownership percentages, and contributions of all limited partners (UBOs). Upon any transfer of a partnership interest, a notice amending the extra-provincial declaration must be filed with the provincial registry within 15 days; if a non-resident partner is admitted, a Part XIII withholding notification must be provided to the CRA within 30 days. In the master franchise context, the general partner must maintain a central UBO ledger identifying every partner holding at least 10% of the partnership interests and must re-verify this information annually for the registered office.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (Capital Contributions and Withdrawals)
Register of General Partners (Identity, Service of Process, and Notices)
Minute Book of the General Partner

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 28% federal general corporate rate; 9% federal small business rate; the LP is fiscally transparent (pass-through) so no entity-level CIT; partners taxed on allocated income
